newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks gain, Ldn peaks despite rate rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks gain, Ldn peaks despite rate rise.

text.p: London stocks surged to a trading record on Thursday after a small interest rate rise ended market uncertainty and other European bourses chalked up healthy gains on the back of a strong overnight performance on Wall Street.

In currency markets, sterling fell after the Bank of England raised rates to 7.0 from 6.75 percent, saying they were now at levels consistent with government inflation targets. Traders took this as a signal that rates had peaked and dumped pounds.

London shares, which had a volatile morning session because of jitters over interest rates, roared ahead by nearly one percent to an intra-day peak of 5,070.7 points on the FTSE index after the rate hike.

Dealers said the central bank's statement that the increase, the fourth in as many months, put rates at a level consistent with an inflation target of 2.5 percent reassured investors and helped the market higher.
"It's comforting as it's probably meant to be that there won't be any more rises in the short term," said a dealer.
The rebound lifted London stocks from negative territory, into which they had fallen after opening at an earlier record high with investors agonising over the effect of a rate rise on sterling.

London shares' bull run has been prompted by a weakening of the pound from recent peaks, which is seen improving profits for exporters. But in the event the small rate increase was shrugged off -- and breathed new life into equities.
Bank shares also staged a rally on the view that the rate move secured a good environment for further robust earnings growth.
Abbey National rose 7-1/2p to 850p and Lloyds TSB Group 8-1/2p to 775-1/2p. Barclays roared to new highs, up 110p to 1,437-1/2p, boosted mainly by results and news of a bigger share buy-back.

In Frankfurt, stocks soared by two percent at one stage, lifted by Wall Street's record close at 8,259.51 points on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, up 71.77. The dollar's advance also helped underpin the market.
Dealers said the German share market had a positive undertone and looked for further gains during the session despite modest losses in the German debt market.
The market focus remained on banking shares with Deutsche Bank among the top volume shares, rising 3.05 marks to 119.75, amid speculation about further banking industry mergers or takeovers.
The Paris bourse, which ended nearly two percent higher on Wednesday, made further gains, adding one percent by midday. It was bolstered by Wall Street and receding interest rate worries.
On currency markets, the dollar climbed half a pfennig to 1.8800 marks, near its highest levels against the German currency since October 1989.
Concern about the potential for trade tensions between the United States and Japan was kept alive by remarks made on Wednesday by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky.

These worries nudged the dollar down from earlier gains to 12-week highs against the Japanese currency. By lunchtime in Europe it was at 118.45 yen, compared with 118.61 in late trade the previous day.
But sterling was the big loser, slipping nearly two pfennigs to 2.9975 marks from 3.0135 just before the Bank of England announcement. It also fell to $1.5933 from $1.6043 late on Wednesday.

Dealers said the market had been split about the chances of a rate rise at this week's meeting and a scaling back of rate rise expectations just prior to the meeting had seen sterling retreat to below 3.00 marks and $1.60.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8800 marks and 118.45 yen, compared with 1.8748 and 118.61 in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 40.2 points at 5,066.4.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 78.96 points at 4,414.35 in bourse trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 30.14 points at 3,067.23
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $318.95 an ounce, compared to $319.85 at the close on Wednesday. Silver was two cents lower at $4.35.
